opportunities.title: Modular marine supply
opportunities.commercialLogic: Component supply can be paired with configuration support and lifecycle service.
opportunities.partnerBenefit: The partner expands its product range with a marine-ready supply path.
opportunities.companyContribution: Tideframe contributes the module architecture and application workflow.
opportunities.partnerContribution: Kestrel Forge contributes industrial context, supplier discipline, and channel hypotheses.

salesCase.need: Builders need configurable marine modules without recreating the interface for every program.
salesCase.alternative: They source disconnected components and absorb integration risk in each build.
salesCase.scaleBasis: A common module family could serve several fictional platform variants.
salesCase.mechanism: A stable interface and configuration guide make the module repeatable across builds.
salesCase.outcome: Builders can evaluate a clearer supply path with fewer bespoke handoffs.
salesCase.ambition: Create a dependable module supply business that compounds across platforms and service channels.
salesCase.entryPoint: A bounded module definition and interface review.
salesCase.evidenceBoundary: Fictional concept only; no supplier qualification, production capacity, or field performance is evidenced.

opportunities.title: Build-and-license pathway
opportunities.payer: Licensees paying for design support and rights
opportunities.commercialLogic: License access can be combined with engineering support, acceptance criteria, and optional component supply.
opportunities.partnerBenefit: The partner can enter a new category while keeping regional manufacturing ownership explicit.
opportunities.companyContribution: Tideframe contributes the design system, training concept, and integration guardrails.
opportunities.partnerContribution: Kestrel Forge contributes manufacturing capability hypotheses and regional execution context.
opportunities.nextQuestion: What must remain controlled by the licensor versus the regional builder?

salesCase.need: Regional builders need a credible way to enter marine products without starting with an empty design sheet.
salesCase.alternative: They either develop slowly in-house or license a black box with little adaptation support.
salesCase.scaleBasis: A controlled build system can be adapted across selected regional product families.
salesCase.mechanism: A license package combines design rules, acceptance gates, and support rather than only a drawing set.
salesCase.outcome: Builders gain a more navigable path from design intent to local production.
salesCase.ambition: Establish a regional build-and-license network with consistent product language and support.
salesCase.entryPoint: A fictional boundary-of-control workshop and sample license architecture.
salesCase.evidenceBoundary: Fictional concept only; licensing terms, engineering validation, and regional approvals are unresolved.

opportunities.title: Distribution and service channel
opportunities.product: A marine product distribution and service program
opportunities.customer: Fictional operators reached through industrial channels
opportunities.payer: Operators buying products and service coverage
opportunities.commercialLogic: Channel sales can be extended by training, spares, commissioning support, and recurring service.
opportunities.partnerBenefit: The partner converts existing channel trust into a lifecycle marine offer.
opportunities.companyContribution: Tideframe contributes service design, commissioning workflow, and support playbooks.
opportunities.partnerContribution: Kestrel Forge contributes distributor relationships and after-sales operating discipline.
opportunities.nextQuestion: Which channel capability should anchor the first serviceable product?

salesCase.need: Operators need marine products that come with a clear local support path, not a box at the dock.
salesCase.alternative: They rely on generalist distributors and assemble support only after a failure.
salesCase.scaleBasis: A trained channel can carry several compatible products and service tiers.
salesCase.mechanism: Distribution is paired with commissioning, spares, and scheduled support responsibilities.
salesCase.outcome: Operators see a more accountable path from purchase to continued use.
salesCase.ambition: Build a regional distribution-and-service network that makes marine products easier to adopt.
salesCase.entryPoint: A fictional channel capability map and service-boundary review.
salesCase.evidenceBoundary: Fictional concept only; channel demand, service capacity, and support economics are not evidenced.

brief.audienceDecision: Select one independent route for a bounded industrial design conversation.
brief.partnerRelevance: Kestrel Forge can add industrial discipline and channels; Tideframe can supply marine-native product and service logic.
brief.partnerThesis: Kestrel Forge and Tideframe could test three independent paths without forcing supply, license, and service into one blended transaction.
brief.companyDifference: Tideframe starts from the marine customer job and carries the operating boundary through product, build, and service.
brief.combinationAdvantage: Kestrel brings industrial repeatability; Tideframe brings marine-specific interfaces and lifecycle context.
brief.strategicUpside: A first route can establish a platform for adjacent marine categories while preserving distinct contracts and channel roles.

blocks.text: Industrial reach can open three different marine businesses
FICTIONAL CONCEPT — internal review only; no deployment, measurements, or approval.
Kestrel brings industrial discipline and channels; Tideframe keeps each marine path commercially distinct.
Supply
Repeatable modules give builders a clearer way to buy marine capability.
Build + license
Regional manufacturers get a controlled path from design intent to local production.
Distribution + service
A product becomes more adoptable when commissioning and support have an owner.
Why this partner
Industrial trust is useful only when the marine customer job remains visible.
Choose one route for a bounded design review; do not imply a bundled agreement.
Marine-native product logic survives the handoff to industry
FICTIONAL CONCEPT — internal review only; no deployment, measurements, or approval.
Tideframe keeps marine need visible as industry adds repeatability.
Module
A stable interface makes supply repeatable.
Build system
Rules and gates travel with the license.
Service path
Support roles remain visible after sale.
Explicit control: design intent, build rights, channel, service boundaries.
Configuration and support logic connect product choices to the marine job.
Supply, license, and service are separate commercial paths with separate buyers.
Industrial customer
Builders, regional manufacturers, and operators have different jobs.
Partner leverage
Kestrel can select the route that matches its strongest capability.
Route discipline: marine need first, industrial mechanism second.
Three independent paths from supply to service
FICTIONAL CONCEPT — internal review only; no deployment, measurements, or approval.
These are not stages of one deal. Each path has a distinct customer, payer, and operating promise.
Supply modules
Repeatable component program for builders.
Build + license
Controlled design system for regional makers.
Distribution + service
Channel route with lifecycle support.
A first route can prove a relationship without erasing the other two businesses.
Make the interface repeatable for the builder
FICTIONAL CONCEPT — internal review only; no deployment, measurements, or approval.
Builders need marine modules that do not recreate integration risk on every platform.
Disconnected sourcing
Components arrive separately and the builder owns the hidden interface work.
Module program
A stable interface and configuration guide create a repeatable supply product.
The customer job is to buy a module with a clear boundary, not a new integration project.
Tideframe carries the marine interface into Kestrel’s industrial supply discipline.
Qualitative comparison only — fictional route framing, with no supplier or performance evidence.
License a build system, not a black box
FICTIONAL CONCEPT — internal review only; no deployment, measurements, or approval.
Regional builders need design intent, acceptance gates, and support together; a license package makes control explicit.
A buildable offer
The licensed product is a marine build system with a clear customer and boundary.
A strategic route
Regional makers reach local production; Kestrel extends reach with control points visible.
Proof boundary: fictional license architecture; terms, engineering validation, and regional approvals remain unresolved.
Put support inside the product promise
FICTIONAL CONCEPT — internal review only; no deployment, measurements, or approval.
Operators need a local support path, so distribution, commissioning, spares, and service must be designed together.
Name the buyer
Operators buy a supported marine product, not only a unit on a list.
Assign the channel
Kestrel’s distributor context can anchor commissioning and after-sales roles.
Make it recurring
A service program turns adoption into a lifecycle relationship.
Options remain open: resale only, trained service channel, or a fuller lifecycle program.
Choose the route that fits the partner’s real capability
FICTIONAL CONCEPT — internal review only; no deployment, measurements, or approval.
Kestrel need not choose all three paths; start where industrial strength meets a clear buyer.
Supply when repeatability leads
Choose a component boundary when builders need a dependable interface.
License when reach leads
Choose build rights when regional production is the partner’s advantage.
Service when channels lead
Choose lifecycle support when operator trust is the differentiator.
Entry: route-selection workshop. Ambition: a repeatable marine category with the right owner.
Select one independent path
FICTIONAL CONCEPT — internal review only; no deployment, measurements, or approval.
Industrial reach is the prize; choose one route to define.
Partner value
Kestrel can test where its supply, manufacturing, or channel strength creates the cleanest leverage.
Company difference
Tideframe keeps the marine customer job and operating boundary intact.
Independent economics
Each route preserves its own buyer, payer, and commercial logic.
Invite a fictional route session: choose the buyer, define the boundary, and name the next proof question.
Fictional investment companion • no investment ask
